newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah easier after U.S. strike on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah easier after U.S. strike on Iraq.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was easier in late trading on Tuesday following news that the United States had launched a missile attack against Iraq, dealers said.
"The news of the U.S strike prompted players, mostly from Singapore, to sell the rupiah and buy dollars," one large local bank dealer said.

The news breifly jolted the market which had been quiet and featureless since Monday, he said. The dealer said, however, it was somewhat of a knee-jerk reaction and the market still needed time to fully interpret the news.
Spot rupiah was last at 2,343.70/44.25, compared with an opening of 2,342.50/43.00.
"The U.S. strike on Iraq has in fact weakened sentiment on the rupiah, but the impact was relatively slight," another foreign bank dealer said.
He said trading volumes were relatively thin as most operators were waiting for Indonesia's latest economic indicators to be announced at the monthly cabinet meeting on Wednesday.
The dealer said the dollar-rupiah rate was likely to range between 2,343.50 and 2,344.50 on Wednesday.
Today and tomorrow was last at 2,341.85/2,342.25 and 2,343.40/44.00 respectively.
One-month swap at 18.20/18.50, two at 35.25/35.50, three at 52.75/53.00 and six at 105.00/106.00 points.
The central bank set its intervention rate at 2,341/2,459 and the conversion rate at 2,341/2,387 on Monday.
